title: Prediction: LIGO O4b and O5 ringdown stacks show dispersive echoes

statements.text: Stacked post-merger ringdowns in LIGO O4b and O5, with reflectivity $R_0 \gtrsim 0.03$ and shear relaxation time $\tau_s \sim 10^{-3}$ s, favor a dispersive echo template over a clean Kerr ringdown with a Bayes factor of at least $10^2$ at a false-positive rate of 10 percent.
statements.conditions: The July 2026 rebuild withdrew the mock-anchored O4 posterior of the March 2026 program, since no public joint analysis produced it. No source reports an outcome.
statements.falsification_criteria: GW stacks favor $R_0$ or $\tau_s$ outside the prior region consistent with O3 and EHT, for example $R_0 \gtrsim 0.1$ with a millisecond $\tau_s$, or a verified EHT ring modulation $\delta I / I \geq 10^{-4}$ at the GW-favored $\tau_s$.

prediction.resolution_criterion: A hierarchical analysis of stacked O4b and O5 post-merger ringdowns with shared $(\epsilon, R_0, \tau_s)$ returns a Bayes factor of at least $10^2$ for the dispersive template over clean Kerr at a false-positive rate of 10 percent.

sources.quote: With R0 ≳ 0.03, τs ∼ 10−3 s, the dispersive template beats clean Kerr with Bayes factor ≥ 102 at FPR = 10%.
The earlier mock-anchored posterior is removed because no public joint analysis produced it.
